hypothesis: A source-test prefix can omit necessary explicit cleanup. Retaining applicable original finalization statements should remove this construction artifact without removing the earlier defect observation.
comparison: Compare full candidate JSON sequences and all source-input receipts. Run only parents whose constructed program sequences changed; byte-identical parents keep their original round19 evidence and are not claimed as freshly executed.
recognized_forms: Python os.remove(local_path) or os.unlink(local_path) through resolved imports
Go localResource.Close(), including a resolved testify NoError adapter
guards: Use only whole top-level source statements.
Retain an unconditional local resource binding before the cut.
Refuse finalization when the resource is rebound in the discarded suffix.
Do not copy cleanup for a resource whose acquisition was discarded.
Retain existing oracle edits on copied cleanup statements.
Preserve input edits and verify emitted test AST before execution.
limitations: Method names identify possible finalizers; this is not a verified lifecycle specification.
Unknown disposal protocols, conditional resource acquisition and escaped aliases remain unsupported.
A new complete test still needs semantic review.
This is a construction delta on a selected calibration cohort, not a 17-trial detector run.
tests: 13 focused tests passed. One executable toy checks that the shortened test closes its resource without repeating acquisition; other tests cover binding changes, removed acquisitions, Go adapters and retained oracle revisions.
unused_preparation_explanation: No native/provider execution. Refrozen after retaining cleanup oracle edits and adding exact unchanged-program delta selection.
findings: The N08 first prefix now passes after its original Close statement is retained; the artificial leaktest failure disappears.
Its next prefix fails the existing unjustified cross-database metric equality. The cleanup repair does not make that oracle valid.
The N04 safe-import witness remains valid and fails at the same contract violation.
This isolates a construction repair, not a recall or precision improvement for an end-to-end detector.
